study type: Prospective Observational Study with Deep Learning Model Development and Validation
cohort: The study included 91 pregnant women (54 with spontaneous labors) providing continuous skin temperature data, with a subset of 28 pregnancies also providing daily steroid hormone samples.
finding: A deep learning model using continuous skin temperature data predicted labor start for 79% of spontaneous labors within a 4.6-day window at 7 days before true labor, with its average prediction error dropping below 2 days at 8 days before labor.
mod_finding: Spontaneous labors exhibited a greater estriol to α-pregnanediol ratio, lower body temperature, and more stable circadian rhythms compared to pregnancies that did not undergo spontaneous labor.
gest_age: Spontaneous labors included in the model training occurred between 34 and 42 weeks of gestation, with input data starting from a gestational age of 240 days until labor onset.
